stem:
Ira looks at the diagram. Points $B$ and $C$ are fixed. She needs every point that is $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ from $B$ and also $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ from $C$.

Which claim correctly locates those points?

options.text: They are the intersection points of the circle of radius $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ centered at $B$ with the circle of radius $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ centered at $C$.
Call the answer the single label midpoint of $BC$.
Say that the finished intersection points are what create the equal $5\,\mathrm{cm}$ distances.
Choose the points only because the printed $5$ is the largest number on the page.

teacher.key_rationale: Equal distance 5 cm from B and from C means the intersection of the two radius-5 circles. Naming midpoint alone, reversing intersections as the cause of the distances, or grabbing the printed 5 miss that locus.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as two equal-radius circles about B and C with intersection points P and Q.
